text: This is AdForge. You type one sentence about what you want to advertise, and it builds the whole ad campaign. Here is a real run, from start to finish.
The sentence: get remote workers in Austin to subscribe to Bean Drop, a forty dollar a month cold brew delivery.
First, a brief. Anything the sentence did not say, like the budget or the offer, is written down as an assumption instead of being guessed silently.
Then research on the live web. Seven real searches find the closest competitors, their pricing and their ad angles, with a source link for every audience insight.
Opus writes the strategy: one big idea, three audience segments with Meta targeting, a budget split, and a brand kit.
Next come the Meta and Google ads. Models cannot count characters, so code checks every headline against the platform limit and sends exact violations back.
For the visuals, a headless browser searches Pinterest. Opus studies the boards, lists the cliches every coffee ad uses, and writes three very different visual styles.
Each ad gets three designs, written as HTML and rendered in a real browser. If any message text lands off the canvas or under another element, the browser measures it and the design goes back.
A harsh judge scores every design on stop power, legibility and brand fit. The winner gets a polish, and the polish has to beat the original head to head. Here, two polishes lost.
Before launch, a critic opens the actual images and checks the copy and ad policy. It failed all five assets, and a fix round repaired only what it flagged.
It also builds the landing page, with the lead form wired in by code, not left to the model.
The result is a launch kit: budgets per channel, tracked links, a Meta upload sheet, a Google Ads Editor sheet, the campaign file, and every final image.
Thirty three model steps, from one sentence. The code is on GitHub, and the full replay is live at adforge replay dot vercel dot app.
